concepts.name: logic
concepts.description: A formal language for making assertions about the world, consisting of a knowledge base and rules of inference.

concepts.name: knowledge_base
concepts.description: A collection of sentences in the language of logic, assumed to be correct and complete.

concepts.name: inference_rule
concepts.description: A rule applied to a knowledge base to derive new, valid conclusions. Must be sound (derive only valid conclusions) and complete (derive all valid conclusions).

concepts.name: logical_sentence
concepts.description: A statement in the language of logic, such as an if-then statement or a predicate.

concepts.name: predicate
concepts.description: A function that maps object arguments to a truth value (True or False). E.g., Feathers(animal).

concepts.name: implicative_relationship
concepts.description: A logical relationship where one statement implies another (A => B).

concepts.name: conjunction
concepts.description: A logical AND operation (^). True only if all statements are true.

concepts.name: disjunction
concepts.description: A logical OR operation (v). True if at least one statement is true.

concepts.name: negation
concepts.description: A logical NOT operation (¬). Inverts the truth value of a statement.

concepts.name: truth_table
concepts.description: A table listing all possible truth values for a logical expression.

concepts.name: logical_property
concepts.description: Properties of logical operations, such as Commutative, Distributive, and Associative.

concepts.name: de_morgans_law
concepts.description: A rule for logical equivalence: ¬(A ^ B) <=> (¬A v ¬B) and ¬(A v B) <=> (¬A ^ ¬B).

concepts.name: implication_elimination
concepts.description: A rule for logical equivalence: (A => B) <=> (¬A v B).

concepts.name: predicate_calculus
concepts.description: First-order logic. An extension of propositional logic that includes variables and quantifiers.

concepts.name: quantifier
concepts.description: A symbol specifying the quantity of elements for which a predicate is true. (e.g., universal quantifier ∀, existential quantifier ∃).

concepts.name: resolution_theorem_proving
concepts.description: A method to prove logical statements by refutation, requiring CNF.

concepts.name: conjunctive_normal_form
concepts.description: Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF). A logical sentence that is a conjunction of clauses, where each clause is a disjunction of literals.

concepts.name: clause
concepts.description: A disjunction of one or more literals.

concepts.name: literal
concepts.description: An atomic formula (predicate) or its negation.

concepts.name: modus_ponens
concepts.description: Rule of inference: (P => Q, P) |- Q. (If P implies Q, and P is true, then Q is true).

concepts.name: modus_tollens
concepts.description: Rule of inference: (P => Q, ¬Q) |- ¬P. (If P implies Q, and Q is false, then P is false).

concepts.name: problem_domain
concepts.description: A specific problem scenario used to illustrate a logical task.

concepts.name: robot_factory_problem
concepts.description: A problem domain where a robot must determine if a widget is liftable.

concepts.name: robot_bird_problem
concepts.description: A problem domain where a robot must identify if an animal is a bird.

concepts.name: object
concepts.description: A physical or conceptual entity in a problem domain.

concepts.name: proof_result
concepts.description: The outcome of a proof, typically true (contradiction found) or false (no contradiction found).

relations.name: implies
relations.description: Represents a logical implication between two logical sentences.

instances.name: RTP_Box_KB_1
instances.description: If a box cannot move, then it is not liftable.

instances.name: RTP_Box_KB_2
instances.description: If a box cannot move and the battery is full, then it is not liftable.

instances.name: RTP_Bird_KB_1
instances.description: If an animal has wings and does not have fur, it is a bird.

instances.name: MP_Bird_Rule
instances.description: If an animal has feathers, it implies the animal is a bird.
